title: Why So Slow? Inclined Planes Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A child rides down a slide, rain runs off a roof, a truck rolls downhill. Gravity pulls each one straight down, yet they all move along a slope. Aarav stops pedalling at the top of the college road and coasts down, speeding up far slower than a falling stone. Why? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we split the weight along a slope.

On a live motion notebook a block slides down a tilting slope at 30, 60 and 10 degrees. A slow-mo replay splits mg into mg sin theta along the slope and mg cos theta into it, with a live readout and an acceleration vs angle graph whose dot follows the sim. Then a rough slope with kinetic friction, the five-step rule (a = g sin theta; a = g(sin theta - mu_k cos theta) sliding down; g(sin theta + mu_k cos theta) sliding up), why the mass cancels, two pause-and-think questions, a worked example on a 3-4-5 ramp, the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.
